title: Which shapes write each of five numbers in base five?
description: Five numbers go on the board one after another, and each is broken into the base five shapes by taking the biggest shape that fits. The working uses the same way as the solved example in the book, and every answer is added back to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: for each number, take the biggest landmark that fits, count it, subtract, and move down one shape. Watch for students who forget that an empty shape is simply left out, as in six hundred fifty one.

video_script.why: The child applies the biggest-landmark-first method of the solved example to five numbers.
video_script.substitution: The numbers fifteen, fifty, one hundred thirty seven, two hundred ninety three and six hundred fifty one replace eighty nine.
video_script.anchor: the book's base five shapes: triangle 1, square 5, hexagon 25, circle 125, wave 625
video_script.payoff_line: Fifteen is three squares, and fifty is two hexagons.

final_answer.value: 15: 3 squares; 50: 2 hexagons; 137: 1 circle, 2 squares, 2 triangles; 293: 2 circles, 1 hexagon, 3 squares, 3 triangles; 651: 1 wave, 1 hexagon, 1 triangle
final_answer.spoken: fifteen is three squares, fifty is two hexagons, one hundred thirty seven is one circle, two squares and two triangles, two hundred ninety three is two circles, one hexagon, three squares and three triangles, and six hundred fifty one is one wave, one hexagon and one triangle

hold_back: 15: 3 squares; 50: 2 hexagons; 137: 1 circle, 2 squares, 2 triangles; 293: 2 circles, 1 hexagon, 3 squares, 3 triangles; 651: 1 wave, 1 hexagon, 1 triangle
maths_rules: triangle 1, square 5, hexagon 25, circle 125, wave 625; each is 5 times the one before
137: 125 fits once; 137 - 125 = 12; 2 x 5 = 10; 12 - 10 = 2: 1 circle, 2 squares, 2 triangles
651: 625 once; 651 - 625 = 26; 25 once; 26 - 25 = 1: 1 wave, 1 hexagon, 0 circles, 0 squares, 1 triangle
video_script.design: One idea: biggest shape first, for five numbers in turn. The shape values stay at the top of the board while each number is worked below.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the base five shapes.
<bookmark mark='shapes'/>A triangle is one, a square is five, and a hexagon is twenty five. <bookmark mark='circle'/>A circle is one hundred twenty five, and a wave is six hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must write five numbers with these shapes. They are fifteen, fifty, one hundred thirty seven, two hundred ninety three and six hundred fifty one.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Which shapes will fifteen need?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with fifteen highlighted

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: five of one shape slide into the next bigger shape, all along the row; a rule line: biggest shape that fits first

marks.five: five of each shape slide into the next shape up
marks.rule: the rule biggest shape that fits first appears under the row

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Each shape is worth five of the shape before it.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. Take the biggest shape that fits, count it, and move down one shape.

marks.given: the shape values and the five numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five shapes worth one, five, twenty five, one hundred twenty five and six hundred twenty five.

beats.on_screen: To find: each number in shapes

marks.find: the words each number in shapes are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each of the five numbers with these shapes.

beats.on_screen: 15: 25 > 15, so start with 5; 3 x 5 = 15, nothing left, 3 squares. 50: 2 x 25 = 50, nothing left, 2 hexagons

marks.fifteen: 3 x 5 = 15 appears and three squares are drawn
marks.fifty: 2 x 25 = 50 appears and two hexagons are drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Step one, fifteen and fifty. Twenty five is more than fifteen, so we start with five. Three times five is fifteen, with nothing left.
<bookmark mark='fifty'/>For fifty, two times twenty five is fifty, so it needs two hexagons and nothing else.

marks.circle: one circle appears and 137 - 125 = 12 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='circle'/>Step two, one hundred thirty seven. A circle fits once. One hundred thirty seven take away one hundred twenty five leaves twelve.
<bookmark mark='squares'/>Twenty five is too big for twelve. Two times five is ten, so two squares.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Twelve take away ten leaves two, which is two triangles.

marks.circles: 2 x 125 = 250 appears with two circles and 293 - 250 = 43
marks.rest: 3 x 5 = 15 and 18 - 15 = 3 appear with three squares and three triangles

narration: <bookmark mark='circles'/>Step three, two hundred ninety three. Two times one hundred twenty five is two hundred fifty, and three would be too many. That leaves forty three.
<bookmark mark='hex'/>One hexagon fits in forty three, and forty three take away twenty five leaves eighteen.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Three times five is fifteen, which leaves three. That gives three squares and three triangles.

beats.on_screen: 651: 625 once; 651 - 625 = 26; 25 once; 26 - 25 = 1; no circles, no squares

marks.tri: one triangle appears; the circle and square places stay empty

narration: <bookmark mark='wave'/>Step four, six hundred fifty one. A wave fits once. Six hundred fifty one take away six hundred twenty five leaves twenty six.
<bookmark mark='hex'/>One hexagon fits, and twenty six take away twenty five leaves one.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>That is one triangle. There are no circles and no squares, so we leave them out.

marks.check: the sum for 137 is written and ticked
marks.check2: the sum for 293 is written and ticked
marks.check3: the sum for 651 is written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, put each answer back into its number. One hundred twenty five plus ten plus two is one hundred thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>Two hundred fifty plus twenty five plus fifteen plus three is two hundred ninety three.
<bookmark mark='check3'/>Six hundred twenty five plus twenty five plus one is six hundred fifty one.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 15: 3 squares; 50: 2 hexagons; 137: 1 circle, 2 squares, 2 triangles; 293: 2 circles, 1 hexagon, 3 squares, 3 triangles; 651: 1 wave, 1 hexagon, 1 triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Fifteen is three squares, and fifty is two hexagons.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>One hundred thirty seven is one circle, two squares and two triangles.
<bookmark mark='rest2'/>Two hundred ninety three is two circles, one hexagon, three squares and three triangles.
<bookmark mark='rest3'/>Six hundred fifty one is one wave, one hexagon and one triangle.
